title: The King's Second Shadow
logline: When King Maelor Varn's shadow begins acting on its own inside the royal palace, Queen Iselde, her brilliant scholar-wife Lady Rosalind, and their precocious eight-year-old child Prince Leo must use empirical science, witty deduction, and hilarious castle contraptions to unravel an ancient court mystery before darkness claims the throne.

episode_outline.title: The Shadow Moves First
episode_outline.summary: During a grand royal feast, King Maelor's cast shadow raises its goblet before he does. While the king confides in Captain Doran, eight-year-old Prince Leo measures the light angle with a protractor, noticing the shadow violates the laws of light. That night a treasury guard is found fallen, and Lady Rosalind discovers the locked door was opened with a hidden counter-lever.

episode_outline.title: The Law of Reflection
episode_outline.summary: Terrified by the shadow's whispers, Maelor seeks advice. Lady Rosalind arrays polished silver mirrors across the throne room to triangulate the shadow's focal point, explaining specular reflection. Prince Leo accidentally blinds Chancellor Pell with a reflected sunbeam while Pell tries to present the royal tax audit.

episode_outline.title: The Pinhole Inquisitor
episode_outline.summary: Prince Leo converts the darkened treasury vault into a giant Camera Obscura. The inverted projected image on the wall proves the Shadow slipped through an eighth-inch keyhole gap. Rosalind explains focal length and inverted light rays, while Doran worries about the security of the kingdom's keyholes.

episode_outline.title: Prism of the First Dynasty
episode_outline.summary: Lady Rosalind unearths an ancient quartz prism from the archives. Splitting sunlight into the visible color spectrum, she discovers the Shadow absorbs ultraviolet and red light, emitting a strange violet phosphorescence. Prince Leo asks the Shadow if violet is its favorite color, prompting a sarcastic retort from the wall.

episode_outline.title: The Courtyard Gnomon
episode_outline.summary: At exact solar noon, every shadow in the castle courtyard points north—except King Maelor's, which points directly at the Forgotten Tower. Leo and Rosalind explain Earth's axial rotation, solar noon, and sundials, turning Maelor's existential dread into an impromptu courtyard science lecture.

episode_outline.title: The Double Penumbra
episode_outline.summary: When Doran lights two battle torches, Maelor casts an umbra and two distinct penumbras—but the Shadow detaches from the penumbra entirely. Rosalind explains light diffusion and partial shadows, while Leo uses hand puppets to project hilarious rabbit ears behind Chancellor Pell's back.

episode_outline.title: The Monocle of Pell
episode_outline.summary: Prince Leo borrows Chancellor Pell's reading monocle without asking and combines it with a crystal lens to build a refracting spyglass. Looking at the vaulted ceiling, he spots secret glyphs etched in the stones. Rosalind explains convex magnification while Pell frantically searches for his missing spectacles.

episode_outline.title: Phosphor and Footprints
episode_outline.summary: To map the Shadow's midnight movements, Prince Leo dusts the hallway floors with crushed fluorite and calcite. When the Shadow glides past, it excites the minerals into glowing green bioluminescence. Queen Iselde applauds the forensic trap, while Doran grumbles about cleaning glowing dust from his boots.

episode_outline.title: The Low-Light Threshold
episode_outline.summary: A stormy twilight descends, reducing ambient contrast in the castle. Lady Rosalind explains human retinal biology, comparing rod and cone photoreceptors. The Shadow emerges from the twilight gloom with a witty riddle regarding the foundation stones of the First Dynasty.

episode_outline.title: The Mirror of Ash
episode_outline.summary: Old Nessa reveals an ancient volcanic obsidian mirror. Lady Rosalind explains volcanic glass formation and internal total reflection. When Queen Iselde and Maelor gaze into the obsidian, they discover the Shadow is not an evil twin, but an ancient solar imprint bound to the throne's geometry.

episode_outline.title: Resonance of the Goblet
episode_outline.summary: King Maelor hears ominous humming whenever he touches his silver goblet. Leo rubs the rim of water-filled crystal glasses, demonstrating sympathetic acoustic resonance and natural frequencies. The team realizes the Shadow is transmitting sound through subterranean granite chambers beneath the banquet hall.

episode_outline.title: The Whispering Gallery
episode_outline.summary: Lady Rosalind investigates the curved elliptical vaulting of the Great Council Hall, demonstrating how sound waves reflect off curved surfaces to create a whispering gallery. She hilariously overhears Chancellor Pell practicing his flattery from forty feet away across the room.

episode_outline.title: The Acid Etching Test
episode_outline.summary: Captain Doran discovers strangely corroded coins in the royal treasury. Lady Rosalind uses citrus juice and vinegar to run an acid-base reactivity test, uncovering a hidden crest etched beneath the silver patina. Leo enthusiastically explains oxidation reactions while Pell frets over damaged coinage.

episode_outline.title: Density of the Crypt Gas
episode_outline.summary: Descending into the deep catacombs, Doran's torch suddenly extinguishes near the floor. Rosalind warns that carbon dioxide is denser than atmospheric air and accumulates in low pockets. Leo deploys a handmade bellows ventilation pump, saving Chancellor Pell from fainting.

episode_outline.title: The Pitch of Dread
episode_outline.summary: An eerie vibration fills the castle, inducing dread among the guards. Lady Rosalind identifies it as 19 Hz infrasound caused by wind blowing across narrow masonry slit windows. Leo adjusts wooden baffles to change the acoustic frequency, turning the terrifying drone into a pleasant royal whistle.

episode_outline.title: The Flame Color Test
episode_outline.summary: Mysterious colored fire erupts from the palace braziers—emerald green and bright lilac. Prince Leo conducts a flame test with Old Nessa's mineral powders, proving the fire was spiked with copper and potassium. Queen Iselde realizes a saboteur is trying to simulate supernatural witchcraft.

episode_outline.title: The Water Clock Conundrum
episode_outline.summary: To calculate the Shadow's appearance times, Prince Leo builds an elaborate clepsydra water clock with calibrated copper floats. He explains fluid discharge rates and gravity flow, discovering the Shadow appears in sync with the underground river's tidal fluctuations.

episode_outline.title: Speed of Sound and Echoes
episode_outline.summary: Lost in the winding catacombs, Maelor and Doran struggle to locate the Shadow's laughter. Rosalind calculates their distance by clapping wooden blocks and timing the echo return, explaining the speed of sound in air. Leo maps the cavern layout using simple acoustic echolocation.

episode_outline.title: The Iron Rust Mystery
episode_outline.summary: Captain Doran finds the iron chains of the inner portcullis corroding at five times normal speed. Rosalind explains electrochemical oxidation and how salt water accelerates iron oxide formation. Leo discovers a bucket of salted brine hidden by a traitorous castle gatekeeper.

episode_outline.title: The Geothermal Spring
episode_outline.summary: Old Nessa fears sulfur vapors from the crypts signal the underworld. Rosalind and Leo explain mineral crystallization and geothermal heat, proving the warm sulfur water comes from a harmless subterranean thermal spring that Leo suggests turning into a royal hot tub.

episode_outline.title: Give Me a Fulcrum
episode_outline.summary: A massive three-ton granite door seals the entrance to the Old Keep. Chancellor Pell insists it requires a battalion of oxen. Leo and Rosalind construct a class-one lever with an iron beam and oak fulcrum, enabling King Maelor to pry the slab open single-handedly to the court's astonishment.

episode_outline.title: The Block and Tackle
episode_outline.summary: To lower Doran into a deep ventilation shaft, Prince Leo rigs a compound pulley system. Leo explains how mechanical advantage divides the load by four. Doran descends effortlessly, though Leo gets distracted by a passing butterfly and leaves the captain suspended mid-air.

episode_outline.title: The Archimedes Screw
episode_outline.summary: Water from an underground conduit threatens to flood the ancient archives. Rosalind and Leo design a wooden Archimedes screw pump. Chancellor Pell is tasked with turning the crank for cardiovascular health, whining about manual labor while successfully clearing the flooded library.

episode_outline.title: Gears of the First Dynasty
episode_outline.summary: Behind the stone door lies a massive bronze gear mechanism. Lady Rosalind explains gear train ratios, angular velocity, and torque. Leo realizes that rotating the smallest 12-tooth gear twelve times will rotate the grand 144-tooth sun dial once, opening the inner sanctum.

episode_outline.title: The Inclined Plane
episode_outline.summary: The court needs to haul heavy stone chests of First Dynasty records up to the laboratory. Leo constructs timber ramps with log rollers, explaining the physics of inclined planes and rolling friction reduction, while Doran marvells that brains can beat brute strength.

episode_outline.title: The Pendulum of Inertia
episode_outline.summary: Rosalind suspends a heavy iron sphere on a fifty-foot cable from the great dome—a giant pendulum. As hours pass, the plane of oscillation slowly rotates, proving Earth's planetary rotation. The Shadow attempts to blow on it, but the law of conservation of angular momentum holds steady.

episode_outline.title: The Center of Gravity
episode_outline.summary: The Shadow perches tauntingly along a razor-thin parapet ledge. Rosalind explains center of mass and base of support to Maelor, while Leo demonstrates equilibrium using a carved toy bird that balances perfectly on its beak. Doran safely maneuvers the ledge using a counterweight pole.

episode_outline.title: Pascal's Liquid Hammer
episode_outline.summary: The team finds an ancient hydraulic locking system pressurized by water columns. Rosalind explains Pascal's law of fluid pressure transmission. Leo uses a narrow piston to effortlessly lift a massive iron deadbolt, demonstrating hydraulic force multiplication.

episode_outline.title: The Wheel and Windlass
episode_outline.summary: Trapped by a falling portcullis, Maelor and Doran must operate a high-ratio wooden windlass. Leo shouts instructions on wheel and axle mechanical advantage, enabling them to hoist the escape platform just before the corridor seals.

episode_outline.title: The Newton's Cradle of Varn
episode_outline.summary: To demonstrate momentum and kinetic energy transfer, Prince Leo constructs a giant suspended cradle using iron cannonballs. When one ball strikes the end, only the opposite ball flies out, teaching Doran and Pell the conservation of momentum in hilarious visual fashion.

episode_outline.title: The Cabbage Juice Indicator
episode_outline.summary: Chancellor Pell suddenly falls ill after sipping imported cordial. Rosalind boils red cabbage into an anthocyanin pH indicator, showing the cordial turns bright teal—indicating an alkaline alkaloid poison. Queen Iselde places the palace on immediate lockdown to find the poisoner.

episode_outline.title: The Shift Cipher
episode_outline.summary: Doran intercepts a coded message tied to a carrier hawk. Prince Leo uses frequency analysis, counting the most common vowels and applying a Caesar shift of four to decode the treasonous letter, uncovering a secret rendezvous in the royal gardens.

episode_outline.title: The Invisible Citrus Ink
episode_outline.summary: A seemingly blank scroll is seized from a suspicious foreign envoy. Rosalind explains organic acid dehydration and carefully warms the parchment over a hearth. Brown caramelized letters appear, revealing an alliance between Duke Vane and the Shadow cult.

episode_outline.title: The Wax Dermal Ridges
episode_outline.summary: Rosalind examines the broken wax seal on the armory ledger. Using fine soot and a camel-hair brush, she dusts the unique friction ridges of a human fingerprint, explaining dermatoglyphics and proving the armory was ransacked by someone within the high court.

episode_outline.title: Willow Bark and Feverfew
episode_outline.summary: When Captain Doran suffers from a throbbing battle headache, Old Nessa and Rosalind prepare an infusion of willow bark. Rosalind explains how salicin provides natural analgesia, bridging folk herbalism with empirical pharmacological science to Pell's amazement.

episode_outline.title: Capillary Action in the Tapestry
episode_outline.summary: A strange dark fluid appears to be climbing upward through the royal tapestries against gravity. Leo demonstrates capillary action and cohesive surface tension using linen strips in colored dye, leading them to discover a hidden conduit behind the stone wall.

episode_outline.title: The Static Electric Amber
episode_outline.summary: During a dry winter night, the iron crown emits tiny crackling blue sparks when touched. Pell cries witchcraft, but Leo rubs polished amber with cat fur to demonstrate electrostatic attraction and electron transfer, delighting Queen Iselde with mini static shocks.

episode_outline.title: The Lodestone's Attraction
episode_outline.summary: Doran's navigation compass spins wildly inside the royal council chamber. Rosalind explains magnetic poles and ferromagnetism. Prince Leo traces the magnetic disturbance to a large lodestone secretly hidden inside the Chancellor's ceremonial footstool.

episode_outline.title: Thermal Expansion of the Gates
episode_outline.summary: On blazing summer afternoons, the fortress gates jam tight, yet they swing loose on freezing nights. Rosalind explains linear thermal expansion of iron. Leo designs an expansion joint gap for the hinges, solving the century-old castle gate dilemma.

episode_outline.title: The Breathing Catacombs
episode_outline.summary: Leo notices green moss thriving in pitch-black catacomb tunnels. Rosalind explains plant respiration, air currents, and photosynthesis, deducing there must be a high-altitude natural ventilation chimney connecting the vault directly to the mountain summit.

episode_outline.title: Triangulation of the Peak
episode_outline.summary: Standing on the castle battlements, Lady Rosalind and Prince Leo use a brass astrolabe to measure stellar elevation angles. Using trigonometric triangulation, they pinpoint the exact mountain coordinates where the First Dynasty constructed their solar observatory.

episode_outline.title: The Speed of Light Hypothesis
episode_outline.summary: King Maelor marvels that the Shadow travels across the courtyard instantaneously. Rosalind explains the astronomical timing of planetary orbits and the finite speed of light, calculating that even the fastest shadow must obey cosmic light propagation.

episode_outline.title: The Parabolic Sun Collector
episode_outline.summary: Anticipating the upcoming celestial event, Prince Leo constructs a large parabolic bronze mirror. He explains how parallel incident rays converge at a single intense focal point, demonstrating its power by boiling water in seconds to Chancellor Pell's utter shock.

episode_outline.title: The Pressure of Bernoulli
episode_outline.summary: Fierce drafts whistle through the castle gatehouse. Rosalind demonstrates Bernoulli's principle by blowing between two sheets of parchment, proving that high fluid velocity creates low pressure. Leo uses the effect to design an airflow stabilizer for the torches.

episode_outline.title: The Syzygy of Three Spheres
episode_outline.summary: Rosalind builds a mechanical orrery illustrating the orbital mechanics of the Sun, Earth, and Moon. She explains solar eclipses and syzygy alignment to Queen Iselde and King Maelor, forecasting a Total Solar Eclipse occurring in exactly three days.

episode_outline.title: The Forensic Tribunal
episode_outline.summary: Armed with chemical test results, cipher decryptions, and fingerprint evidence, Queen Iselde and Lady Rosalind convene a royal court tribunal. Through clear scientific deduction, they unmask the traitorous Duke who used ancient trickery to manipulate the kingdom.

episode_outline.title: The Smoked Glass Corona
episode_outline.summary: The day of the Great Eclipse arrives. Warning the court against irreversible retinal damage from ultraviolet rays, Lady Rosalind and Leo craft protective smoked-glass viewing plates for the royal family, explaining the solar corona and eye safety.

episode_outline.title: The Great Throne Obscura
episode_outline.summary: During totality, the throne room is sealed into a colossal camera obscura. As the moon covers the sun, the Shadow entity reveals its true nature: an ancient sentient projection created by the First Dynasty to record royal wisdom and protect the realm from ignorance.

episode_outline.title: Harmonic Resonance of the Crown
episode_outline.summary: Prince Leo plays the resonant frequencies on his tuned crystal glasses, while Rosalind directs the parabolic bronze mirrors toward the throne. Combining optics, sound resonance, and geometry, King Maelor and the Shadow merge their intentions into harmonic balance.

episode_outline.title: The Light of Varn
episode_outline.summary: Superstition gives way to knowledge across the realm. Queen Iselde and Lady Rosalind charter the Royal Academy of Natural Sciences; Prince Leo is named Chief Junior Inquisitor of Inventions; and King Maelor's shadow becomes an enlightened court companion, projecting witty educational shadow puppets for the cheering children of Varn.
